title: Pick two apples off a potted apple tree by lifting, stems on, and lay them in a picking bucket
instruction: Pick both apples off the tree into the bucket.
context: Picking apples into a bucket is familiar from gardens and pick-your-own orchards. This repeatable practice rig exercises the force-direction choice: tilting combined with draw can detach its magnetic stem cap with the stem retained, whereas a straight AXIAL tug pulls its peg out; then lay it gently in the bucket. This failure ordering is specific to the practice rig, not universal apple biology.
setup: The real-world version is a reusable practice rig. World x forward, y left, z up; table top is z=0 in these setup dimensions. A 25 mm hardwood-dowel artificial trunk rises 500 mm above the table from a 300 mm, 12 L black pot of dry sand and bark mulch, 11.5 kg total. Pot centre is (0.350,-0.100) m. Two printed 25 mm spurs point at azimuths 160 and 250 degrees, carrying 75 mm imitation apples whose complete handled socket/peg/stem/cap assemblies total 180 g with centred COMs at heights 310 and 350 mm. Their centres are approximately (0.273,-0.072) and (0.322,-0.177) m. Each has a 6 x 20 mm TPU95A flexible stem, nominal 19-degree precurve, 12.7 x 3 mm steel cap on a D84 spur magnet (session-check target 40 N) and a 12 mm peg on a D82 socket magnet (24 N). A 16 mm diameter, 30 mm deep open well recesses the 16 x 16.7 mm socket mouth 13 mm below the shoulder; the stem above the socket is not buried. A hollow apple/internal cavity is accessed through a 20 mm calyx port for centred epoxy-secured steel ballast. A 290 mm diameter, 230 mm deep green bucket with 25 mm foam pad stands at (0.200,-0.430) m. Both arms start READY, grippers open; task-local native effort limits are 40 N per finger. CAD, assembly and proposed physical session checks are in README.md and rig/.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, from a photo and from the video. An apple is in the bucket when it rests inside it: its centre inside the bucket's wall (by at least half the apple's radius) and below the rim, sitting on the foam pad or on the other apple (its centre within 1 cm of where it would rest on them). It was dropped if it was let go (no gripper touching it), or came off the tree with no gripper touching it, with its lowest point more than 5 cm above what it then landed on (the pad, the other apple, the pot's soil or rim, the bucket's rim or the table); or if, with no gripper touching it, it came down onto the table from more than 5 cm above it since it was last held or at rest (rolling off the bucket's rim, say); or if it reached the floor. Its stem is on when the stem (with its steel cap) is still in the apple; it is a stem pull when the apple came off without it (the stem stays on the spur). 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: the pot tips over (leans more than 20 degrees from upright). Otherwise, by the state at the end, each apple earns: 0.5 if it is in the bucket, its stem is on, and it was not dropped; 0.25 if it is in the bucket and was not dropped, but its stem pulled out (a stem pull); 0 otherwise: still on the tree, dropped, or outside the bucket. The task score is the sum for the two apples, and 1.0 also needs no gripper touching an apple and both apples still (no point of either apple moving more than 5 mm over the last 1 s), held for 1 s; otherwise the sum is capped at 0.75. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Return pot and bucket to their tape marks, empty the bucket, push pulled-out pegs back into their sockets and reseat both magnetic stem caps. Check the specified seat/peg hold, level and added-weight droop before a physical session. No part is consumed.
fidelity: Practice rig at real size/mass. Per-physics spring wrench and opposite tree wrench: seat tension + bend/6.35mm reaches40N, peg24N. Bending .21Nm/rad with gravity preload; twist slips at cap friction. One hinge replaces distributed stem bending; magnetic hold does not fade before release. Apples/trunk/pad are rigid, leaves noncolliding; drops proxy bruising. Calibration is proposed, not physically measured.
